summary: Candidate is a knowledge_reference at session granularity providing evidence-based design guidance for cache eviction algorithm selection. It is semantically distinct from existing skills: it establishes a foundational principle (quick demotion efficiency) rather than implementing algorithms, tuning parameters, or evaluating performance. The existing skills in the registry (parallel execution, virtual hub routing) are from completely different domains and do not overlap. Peer candidates (S3-FIFO implementation, tuning, evaluation protocol) are at different asset layers (session_skill, macro_protocol) and stages (implementation, configuration, evaluation) and depend on this principle as foundational knowledge. No existing skill in the registry covers cache eviction design principles.
